newsitem.title: UK: UK tightens checks on digital TV access providers.
newsitem.headline: UK tightens checks on digital TV access providers.

text.p: Britain's Department of Trade and Industry said on Tuesday it had introduced new safeguards in regulations governing the supply of conditional access services in digital television.
The safeguards are included in regulations laid in parliament. They will come into force on January 7, 1997.

"The new provision requires information and co-operation to be provided to broadcasters - before services are offered - by any entrant to the digital conditional access market, so that broadcasters can take up his service as soon as it is available," Science and Technology Minister Ian Taylor said.
"It (the Government) supports the clear obligation on all conditional access operators to provide services on fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory terms," he added.
Conditional access is the system for controlling access to broadcast services whereby operators can enable or disable receivers, depending on whether viewers have paid for a service.

Satellite broadcaster BSkyB plans to launch digital satellite services with some 200 channels into the UK in late 1997. A terrestrial version -- offering around 35 channels -- is expected to follow in 1998.
There had been fears that BSkyB, as the first entrant into the market, would be able to control conditional access to the potential harm of competitors.

"We have been conscious all along of the need to balance the incentives for innovation and early investment in developing the digital market with strong safeguards and sanctions against possible anti-competitive abuses of advantages gained by moving first into the market," Taylor said.
Taylor said the regulations formed a milestone in the government's efforts to make the UK a world leader in digital television.

The next regulatory steps would be the publication by Oftel of a draft guidance document on its role in regulating the conditional access regime and the licensing of digital terrestrial multiplex providers and broadcasters by the ITC.
